status: Working requirements draft; hardware acceptance and presentation reconciliation open

presentation.phaseAuthority: Slide 7 delivery order; slides 3–4 proposed science alternatives
presentation.scope: Mission phase extension only; Rev09 mass and geometry unchanged; no Aeolus source incorporation

phases.title: 01 Rideshare
phases.description: Show FREYA carried by the host second stage, then capsule separation. Cold-gas hardware remains on the detachable reentry module.

phases.title: 02 Orient
phases.description: Acquire the burn attitude with optical/MEMS estimation and cold-gas control, then start vehicle telemetry.

phases.title: 03 Deorbit
phases.description: Perform the retrograde burn, confirm its completion and detach the expendable reentry module.

phases.title: 04 Entry
phases.description: The heat shield, aerodynamic shape and low center of gravity support passive entry and deceleration. Do not credit cold-gas control after module jettison.

phases.title: 05 Carrier extraction
phases.description: Remove the cover, deploy the carrier parachute, extract the carrier and discard the aeroshell. Begin the independent carrier telemetry sequence.

phases.title: 06 Probe release
phases.description: Descend to the release gate. Release every probe individually, deploying its own smaller parachute for descent and stabilization.

phases.title: 07 Probe delivery
phases.description: Show nose-first impact and schematic emplacement for every probe. Activate instruments and telemetry using the antenna integrated with retained parachute shrouds.

phases.title: 08 Science operations
phases.description: Acquire soil, run blanks and controls, apply the selected proposed protocol, and inspect detector readout and interpretation. The two source protocols remain alternatives.

phases.title: 09 Data return
phases.source: Presentation slide 7 · probe telemetry; Rev09 SYS-001 and COM-01–05
phases.description: Buffer science and engineering records, repeat the carrier status word, and illustrate an assumed orbiter relay and onward return to Earth.

gas-trap.name: Slide 4 · sealed gas and trap assay
gas-trap.sample: 0.25 cm³ per vessel; proposed 2–5 cm source depth
gas-trap.conditions: No water added; sealed and dark at −10 to 0 °C for 1–5 sols
steps: Soil into test and control vessels
Illustrate acquiring soil from the proposed 2–5 cm source zone and loading 0.25 cm³ into each vessel. This does not demonstrate sample acquisition.
Show no-soil controls and baseline counts, O₂ and pressure before dosing; keep controls distinct from the test vessel.
Illustrate separate ³H₂ and ¹⁴CO test channels and a defined time-zero count. No physical dosing or radioactive hardware is controlled.
Show a compressed incubation review segment: no water added, dark, −10 to 0 °C, 1–5 sols proposed. Playback seconds are not incubation time.
Show gas counting and transfer to cold-water/CO₂ trap detectors. Counts identify retained label; they do not identify a molecule or prove biology.
Illustrate the accounting question for label absent from gas and traps. Leaks and sorption remain alternative explanations; extraction would be needed to identify larger products.
Show test/control comparison and valid non-detection checks. A difference can motivate further investigation; it does not establish life.

extract.name: Slide 3 · incubation and extraction concept
extract.sample: Approximately 1 g soil; sample provenance and controls required
extract.conditions: Near Mars ambient pressure; proposed 0–5 °C incubation
steps: Illustrate approximately 1 g soil alongside heat-treated, no-soil and known-microbe control concepts. These are proposed validation steps.
Record baseline detector and environmental observations and keep controls separate from the unmodified test sample.
Illustrate candidate ¹⁴CO₂, ¹⁴CO, ³H₂ or ³H₂O channels. These are alternative experimental inputs, not a selected flight recipe.
Illustrate near-ambient-pressure incubation at 0–5 °C. Do not merge this temperature or water assumption into the slide 4 gas/trap concept.
Illustrate excess-gas removal, carbonate-control acidification and water-soluble versus oil-soluble extraction concepts. Hardware and sample transfer remain unverified.
Show detector acquisition for retained label in separate fractions, with sensitivity and interference still requiring laboratory validation.
Compare test/control and hydrophobic/hydrophilic behavior. Abiotic incorporation, chemical interference and contamination must be considered before any biological interpretation.

sourceRequirements.text: The mission shall deliver three independent 2.00 kg probes to the Martian surface.  (Established)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The mission shall deliver two independent aeroshell vehicles, each carrying seven 2.00 kg probes.  (Established)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Each vehicle shall remain mechanically and electrically compatible with the approved host upper-stage separation interface.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Each vehicle shall execute a defined separation, orbit determination, deorbit, entry, descent and probe-release sequence.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The mission shall document allowable launch, cruise, orbit and atmospheric entry environments before design freeze.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The mission shall define target landing regions, delivery dispersion and science-site acceptance criteria.  (Proposed assumption; verify by analysis and test) Planning baseline: Assume an initial 100 km-radius target region for A and 50 km-radius for each B vehicle, with 95% of Monte Carlo landings within the respective region; exclude scientifically prohibited terrain.
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The program shall maintain independent mass, power, volume, thermal and delta-v budgets with margins approved at PDR.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The flight system shall implement autonomous safe-state and abort/inhibit logic for premature motor ignition and pyrotechnic deployment.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The nominal aeroshell outer diameter shall be 800 mm.  (Established)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The assembled aeroshell height shall be 600 mm, subject to confirmation of datum and inclusion of the upper cover.  (Established / clarify)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The lower heat shield shall retain the current baseline contour and include a nominal 70 mm radius transition to the upper-shell profile.  (Established / drawing needed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The upper shell shall use aluminum alloy; grade, thickness, insulation and joint design shall be selected by structural and aerothermal analysis.  (Established / derived)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The lower heat shield shall use a qualified ablative thermal-protection system, with material and thickness verified for the orbital-entry trajectory.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The carrier and all stowed probes shall fit within the aeroshell with verified deployment clearance and launch-load restraint.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The upper cover opening shall provide unobstructed passage of the loaded probe carrier during ejection.  (Established)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The aeroshell shall withstand launch, separation, deorbit, entry and deployment load cases with documented positive structural margins.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: All attachments across the heat shield shall preserve TPS integrity; sacrificial external DOM connections shall not require through-holes in the heat shield.  (Established / derived)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The deorbit module shall use one J-class solid rocket motor in the baseline configuration.  (Established)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The vehicle shall provide four reaction wheels for attitude control, with wheel-axis geometry and independent controllability verified.  (Established / verify)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The attitude solution shall fuse inertial MEMS gyro measurements with camera-derived Mars limb or feature observations and available Sun observations.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The vehicle shall inhibit deorbit firing unless attitude, estimated orbit state, predicted entry corridor and propulsion readiness satisfy approved limits.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The deorbit propulsion system shall provide the trajectory-specific required impulse and delta-v with defined dispersions and margin.  (Proposed assumption; verify by analysis and test) Planning baseline: For the assumed 300 km orbit and 50 km vacuum-periapsis proxy, use 60.3 m/s ideal delta-v, with 25% planning margin (75.4 m/s). At 50 kg B wet mass, the impulse-equivalent planning value is 3.77 kN s; actual delivered impulse must be calculated with rocket equation and a motor thrust curve.
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The sacrificial DOM shall mount beneath the heat shield without compromising the thermal-protection barrier.  (Established)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The hybrid-engine trade shall evaluate paraffin fuel, N2O oxidizer, tankage, feed system and ignition against the A solid-motor architecture.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: If selected, the cold-gas attitude system shall include all thrusters, valves, plumbing, regulator and usable N2O/N2 gas mass in the budget.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Attitude control shall account for momentum buildup, wheel saturation, deorbit disturbances and the absence or availability of desaturation actuators.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Orbit and attitude estimation shall demonstrate observability during camera occultation, low-light conditions and changing Mars viewing geometry.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The reference entry trajectory shall originate from approximately 300 km Mars orbit; actual entry interface and flight-path angle shall be determined by trajectory design.  (Established / derived)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The aeroshell shall maintain a thermally and dynamically acceptable entry attitude throughout peak heating and deceleration.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: TPS sizing shall use trajectory-dependent convective and radiative heating, heat soak, ablation and aluminum-shell temperature limits.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Parachute deployment shall occur only within verified Mach number, dynamic pressure and altitude envelopes.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The PCM recovery parachute shall have nominal 1.5 m diameter, pending Mars deployment and descent qualification.  (Established / verify)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The PCM recovery parachute shall use the 2.0 m candidate diameter pending vehicle-level mass and deployment analysis.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The system shall safely separate the heat shield and upper cover in the commanded sequence without collision with the PCM or probes.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The descent system shall determine probe release altitude using a qualified sensing and estimation method with defined uncertainty.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Each probe shall deploy a nominal 0.5 m parachute, subject to terminal-speed and stability verification.  (Established / verify)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The EDL analysis shall account for the low density and variability of the Martian atmosphere, winds, and landing-site elevation.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The PCM shall restrain three probes in vertical stowage until commanded release.  (Established)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Each PCM shall restrain seven probes in vertical stowage until commanded release.  (Established probe count; assumed packaging envelope) Planning baseline: Assume seven vertically stowed probes in a 3+3+1 arrangement. Verify fit inside the 800 mm diameter shell with a CAD swept-volume extraction study and positive clearance at maximum tolerance.
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The PCM shall release probes individually, without mechanical interference, following an altitude-gated release schedule.  (Established / derived)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The PCM shall remain retained through entry until its extraction conditions are met.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The carrier ejection system shall demonstrate cover clearance, parachute extraction and no contact with critical spacecraft elements.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Any pyrotechnic separation device shall have independent electrical inhibits and ground-safe handling provisions.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Release sequencing shall provide an adjustable interval and shall be validated against descent rate, wind drift and probe separation.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Each probe shall have a nominal overall length of 200 mm and main-body diameter of 50 mm.  (Established)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Each probe shall include an upper shoulder of nominal 75 mm diameter over approximately the upper third of its length.  (Established)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Each probe flight mass shall be 2.00 kg including science payload, power, structure, radio, parachute and consumables.  (Established)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Each probe shall retain a pointed lower penetration head and deploy in an attitude that supports near-vertical surface penetration.  (Established / derived)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Each probe shall provide a tether-integrated antenna connection from the center of its upper end.  (Established)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The probe shall protect the science sample and sample pathway from contamination introduced by spacecraft materials or entry heating.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The science system shall execute a documented life-detection measurement protocol with controls, blanks and decision thresholds.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The science system shall obtain, transfer and analyze Martian material with demonstrated sample mass, depth, integrity and instrument sensitivity.  (Proposed assumption; verify by analysis and test) Planning baseline: Assume a 0.5 g minimum collected sample from 20-100 mm below the local surface per probe, with 80% transfer efficiency and duplicate blank/control measurements. These are science-planning targets requiring laboratory validation.
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The probe shall provide energy storage and environmental protection sufficient for the approved post-landing operating duration.  (Proposed assumption; verify by analysis and test) Planning baseline: Assume 24 h A and 72 h B surface operation, with a 20% usable energy margin after temperature derating and communications duty cycle.
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The science and communications system shall operate under defined dust deposition, temperature and illumination cases.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The probe shall demonstrate survival of the predicted impact loads across the defined regolith and ice mechanical-property envelope.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The mission shall define an end-to-end telecommunications path, link budget, data storage and expected data return to Earth.  (Proposed assumption; verify by analysis and test) Planning baseline: Assume a Mars-orbit relay link using a UHF compatible transceiver, onboard buffering of at least 64 MB A / 256 MB B per probe, and at least 95% data retention until relay opportunity; final interoperability depends on relay provider agreement.
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Each probe shall provide unique identification, health telemetry and time-tagged science data.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The program shall determine applicable Mars planetary-protection classification with the responsible authority before flight hardware processing.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Life-detection sample-contacting hardware shall meet the approved biological contamination and recontamination prevention requirements.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The program shall maintain bidirectional traceability from mission objectives through requirements, design, test evidence and anomalies.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Each flight-critical release, ignition, attitude and descent function shall be verified by analysis and representative integrated testing.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The program shall perform thermal-vacuum, vibration, shock, deployment and impact qualification at documented environments.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: The program shall approve a fault tree and hazard controls for propulsion, pressure vessels, pyrotechnics and inadvertent Mars impact.  (Proposed)
sourceRequirements.verification: See source requirement and Section 9; evidence pending

sourceRequirements.text: Provide calibrated camera measurements of the Mars limb/horizon, apparent disk size and identifiable large-scale surface features when visible; estimate attitude and orbital/ground-track state with uncertainty.
sourceRequirements.section: 7A.1 Camera / MEMS / onboard ML navigation and attitude
sourceRequirements.verification: Hardware-in-the-loop image sequences, camera calibration and navigation-error budget.

sourceRequirements.text: Observe the Sun when within the camera field of view and safe sensor exposure limits; fuse Sun-direction observations with Mars observations and inertial data.
sourceRequirements.section: 7A.1 Camera / MEMS / onboard ML navigation and attitude
sourceRequirements.verification: Illumination, occultation and Sun-avoidance simulation; attitude observability analysis.

sourceRequirements.text: Use a MEMS gyroscope/IMU to propagate attitude between optical observations; estimate gyro bias and bound drift when Mars and Sun are temporarily unavailable.
sourceRequirements.section: 7A.1 Camera / MEMS / onboard ML navigation and attitude
sourceRequirements.verification: Sensor calibration, thermal drift tests and outage simulations.

sourceRequirements.text: Run deterministic guidance, navigation and control on a Raspberry Pi-class processor, with ML-assisted Mars limb / landmark detection; safety-critical control shall not rely solely on unverified ML output.
sourceRequirements.section: 7A.1 Camera / MEMS / onboard ML navigation and attitude
sourceRequirements.verification: Processor latency, worst-case execution time, fault injection and independently checked state-estimation performance.

sourceRequirements.text: Control spacecraft attitude using six independently commanded cold-gas thrusters, with verified torque authority about three axes and fault-tolerant command inhibits.
sourceRequirements.section: 7A.1 Camera / MEMS / onboard ML navigation and attitude
sourceRequirements.verification: Thruster geometry and torque matrix, impulse-bit, propellant budget and closed-loop simulations.

sourceRequirements.text: Verify attitude and orbital-state confidence before deorbit ignition; inhibit ignition if navigation confidence, pointing error or thruster health is outside approved limits.
sourceRequirements.section: 7A.1 Camera / MEMS / onboard ML navigation and attitude
sourceRequirements.verification: Monte Carlo deorbit targeting, timing, safe-mode and inhibit tests.

sourceRequirements.text: Define six-thruster implementation as a proposed architecture change. Reconcile against the existing four-reaction-wheel baseline and Configuration B hybrid oxidizer / cold-gas supply; do not assume N2O thrusters share a tank without regulator, phase-state and compatibility qualification.
sourceRequirements.section: 7A.1 Camera / MEMS / onboard ML navigation and attitude
sourceRequirements.verification: Signed trade study and updated P&ID, mass, power and propulsion interface control documents.

sourceRequirements.text: Establish the entry corridor, worst-case heating rate, integrated heat load, dynamic pressure, deceleration, aero-moments and center-of-pressure movement for dispersions in Mars atmosphere and vehicle properties.
sourceRequirements.section: 7A.2 Reentry aerothermal and structural load management
sourceRequirements.verification: Trajectory/CFD/aerothermal analyses with stated margins and uncertainties.

sourceRequirements.text: Size and qualify the ablative heat shield, insulation and aluminum backshell for peak and integrated heat exposure; maintain internal electronics, batteries, PCM and probe temperatures within qualified limits.
sourceRequirements.section: 7A.2 Reentry aerothermal and structural load management
sourceRequirements.verification: Thermal network model, material response, thermal-vacuum and representative heating tests.

sourceRequirements.text: Maintain positive structural margins for peak aerodynamic pressure, deceleration, vibration, thermal gradients, fastener and joint loads, including the 70 mm heat-shield-to-backshell transition.
sourceRequirements.section: 7A.2 Reentry aerothermal and structural load management
sourceRequirements.verification: Finite-element load cases, structural proof and coupled thermal-stress assessment.

sourceRequirements.text: Ensure the external deorbit/hybrid propulsion module does not penetrate the heat shield and that sacrificial attachments cannot cause unacceptable TPS damage, destabilization or debris impact during entry.
sourceRequirements.section: 7A.2 Reentry aerothermal and structural load management
sourceRequirements.verification: Interface drawings, separation dynamics and TPS continuity inspection.

sourceRequirements.text: Demonstrate stable heat-shield-forward entry and adequate control authority before atmospheric interface; prohibit reliance on active cold-gas control after its external hardware is sacrificed.
sourceRequirements.section: 7A.2 Reentry aerothermal and structural load management
sourceRequirements.verification: Six-degree-of-freedom entry stability and control-transition simulations.

sourceRequirements.text: Verify cover release, parachute deployment and PCM ejection only after thermal, dynamic-pressure and deceleration conditions are inside qualified release envelopes.
sourceRequirements.section: 7A.2 Reentry aerothermal and structural load management
sourceRequirements.verification: Event sequencing tests, entry/descent Monte Carlo and separation tests.

sourceRequirements.text: Integrate a low-average-duty-cycle, high-peak-power radio transmitter and energy buffer within the probe carrier, with a defined antenna, receiver/relay target and link budget.
sourceRequirements.verification: RF link analysis including Mars distance, geometry, antenna pointing and peak power draw.

sourceRequirements.text: Transmit the nine-bit cumulative mission-status payload nominally once per 60 seconds; queue events between transmissions and repeat the latest status until carrier power is exhausted or mission complete.
sourceRequirements.verification: Packet encoding and timing tests, outage and reset tests.

sourceRequirements.text: Provide independent energy storage sized for transmitter peak power without browning out avionics or release actuators; limit average consumption by duty cycling.
sourceRequirements.verification: Power integrity, pulse load and battery thermal tests.

sourceRequirements.text: Record event time and confidence locally, protect the latched status word against resets, and distinguish command issuance from sensor-confirmed completion.
sourceRequirements.verification: Fault injection and event confirmation tests.

sourceRequirements.text: Do not credit reception during entry plasma blackout, antenna occlusion or carrier tumbling without validated link analysis; store and retransmit status when a link becomes available.
sourceRequirements.verification: End-to-end link availability and missed-pass analysis.

sourceRequirements.text: The program shall produce a 6-DOF Mars orbit-to-surface trajectory Monte Carlo, including atmospheric dispersions, prior to propulsion selection. Verification: Analysis.
sourceRequirements.verification: Analysis.

sourceRequirements.text: The propulsion design shall demonstrate delivered delta-v and pointing error with a 20 kg initial mass and explicit propulsion margin. Verification: Analysis + test.
sourceRequirements.verification: Analysis + test.

sourceRequirements.text: The aeroshell shall have a validated coupled aerothermal and structural model including 600 mm upper shell, aluminum thermal limits, and 70 mm transition. Verification: Analysis + test.
sourceRequirements.verification: Analysis + test.

sourceRequirements.text: The descent system shall meet qualified deployment Mach, dynamic-pressure, altitude and inflation-load limits; nominal chute diameters alone are not acceptance criteria. Verification: Analysis + test.
sourceRequirements.verification: Analysis + test.

sourceRequirements.text: Each probe shall meet defined impact speed, attitude, penetration-depth and survival envelopes over specified soil/ice conditions. Verification: Test.
sourceRequirements.verification: Test.

sourceRequirements.text: The navigation system shall quantify covariance and observability across periods without camera or Sun visibility. Verification: Simulation + test.
sourceRequirements.verification: Simulation + test.

sourceRequirements.text: Each life-detection measurement shall have documented blanks, contamination budgets, calibration, detection limits and false-positive controls. Verification: Test + review.
sourceRequirements.verification: Test + review.

sourceRequirements.text: The spacecraft shall demonstrate positive power and communication margins for the selected operating duration and geometry. Verification: Analysis + test.
sourceRequirements.verification: Analysis + test.

sourceRequirements.text: The program shall approve an end-to-end planetary protection implementation plan before hardware exposure to flight environments. Verification: Review.
sourceRequirements.verification: Review.

sourceRequirements.text: A complete requirement verification matrix shall define objective pass/fail criteria, owners and evidence for every MIS/STR/GNC/EDL/PCM/PRB/SYS/DER item. Verification: Inspection.
sourceRequirements.verification: Inspection.
